questions.question: What is the standard SI (International System) unit of time?
questions.explanation: The second (s) is the globally accepted standard unit for measuring time.

questions.question: Which of the following is an ancient device used to measure time relying on the sun's shadow?
questions.explanation: A sundial tracks the Earth's rotation by mapping the shifting shadow of a fixed object.

questions.question: If object A covers a certain distance in less time than object B, object A is moving:
questions.explanation: Taking less time for the same distance indicates a higher velocity or speed.

questions.question: What is the mathematical formula used to calculate speed?
questions.explanation: Speed is defined as the rate of change of distance with respect to time.

questions.question: What information does the speedometer on a car's dashboard display?

options.text: The instantaneous speed of the vehicle in km/h

questions.explanation: A speedometer provides real-time feedback on how fast the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: What specific device is used in sports to measure very short time intervals with high accuracy?
questions.explanation: Stopwatches are engineered to start and stop on command to measure precise intervals.

questions.question: The simple, repeating back-and-forth movement of a pendulum is called:
questions.explanation: One complete swing from one extreme to the other and back is an oscillation.

questions.question: Exactly how many seconds are contained in one hour?
questions.explanation: 1 hour = 60 minutes = 60 × 60 = 3600 seconds.

questions.question: A train moving along a straight track covers exactly equal distances in equal intervals of time. This is called:
questions.explanation: Uniform linear motion occurs when speed remains perfectly constant.

questions.question: What instrument measures the total cumulative distance travelled by a vehicle?
questions.explanation: An odometer tracks the total mileage (usually in kilometres) covered by the wheels.

questions.question: A car travels 150 metres in exactly 10 seconds. What is its speed in m/s?
questions.explanation: Using the formula: Speed = 150 m / 10 s = 15 m/s.

questions.question: If a freight train is travelling at a constant 60 km/h, how far will it travel in 3 hours?
questions.explanation: Distance = Speed × Time = 60 km/h × 3 h = 180 km.

questions.question: What exactly defines the "time period" of a simple pendulum?

options.text: The time taken to complete exactly one full oscillation
The time it swings before friction stops it

questions.explanation: This constant duration allows pendulums to be used as reliable timekeepers.

questions.question: A car driving through heavy, stop-and-go city traffic is a classic example of what kind of motion?
questions.explanation: Because the speed constantly fluctuates, the motion is non-uniform.

questions.question: Convert a speed of 36 km/h into meters per second (m/s).
questions.explanation: To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by the factor 5/18. 36 × (5/18) = 10 m/s.

questions.question: Runner A completes 400m in 50s. Runner B completes 400m in 45s. Who is faster?
questions.explanation: Runner B took less time to cover the same distance, resulting in a higher calculated speed.

questions.question: Why is an hourglass (sand clock) practically unsuitable for measuring varying, random short time intervals?

options.text: It only measures one specific, fixed duration of time based on its physical design

questions.explanation: It cannot be started and stopped arbitrarily like a stopwatch.

questions.question: On what physical factor does the time period of a simple pendulum primarily depend?

options.text: The mass of the metallic bob
The length of the suspending string

questions.explanation: Galileo discovered that the period depends squarely on the length, independent of mass.

questions.question: If a vehicle's speed constantly changes during a trip, what formula do you use to find the overall speed?

options.text: Total Distance divided by Total Time (Average Speed)

questions.explanation: Average speed accounts for all variations over the entire journey.

questions.question: A person jogs 1200 m in 8 minutes. What is their speed in standard m/s?
questions.explanation: First, convert time to seconds: 8 × 60 = 480 s. Speed = 1200 / 480 = 2.5 m/s.

questions.question: A train travels 360 km at a constant speed of 25 m/s. How many hours does the journey take?
A galloping horse runs at 18 m/s. A train moves at 72 km/h. Which is travelling faster?

options.text: They are exactly the same speed
The train is twice as fast

questions.explanation: 72 km/h = 20 m/s. Therefore, the train (20 m/s) outpaces the horse (18 m/s).

questions.question: During an experiment, why shouldn't you push a pendulum bob when releasing it?

options.text: It makes the bob fly off
It alters the natural periodic motion, yielding an inaccurate time period
It makes the clock run backward

questions.explanation: Adding an external force disrupts the gravity-driven simple harmonic motion.

questions.question: A vehicle covers 2 km total. For the first 500 m, speed is 10 m/s. For the next 500 m, speed is 5 m/s. The total journey must take 200 s. At what speed must it travel the remaining 1000 m?
questions.explanation: T1=50s, T2=100s. Time used = 150s. Time left = 200 - 150 = 50s. Speed = 1000m / 50s = 20 m/s.

questions.question: Using the data from the previous question, what is the average speed of the vehicle for the ENTIRE 2 km journey?
questions.explanation: Average speed = Total Distance / Total Time = 2000 m / 200 s = 10 m/s.

questions.question: How did the scientist Christiaan Huygens revolutionize timekeeping in 1656?

options.text: He invented the pendulum clock, utilizing predictable periodic motion for high accuracy
He created the first water clock

questions.explanation: He applied Galileo's observations of isochronism to create the first highly accurate mechanical clock.

questions.question: A student records the distance covered by a car: 0s-0m, 10s-8m, 20s-16m, 30s-24m. What specific type of motion is this?
questions.explanation: The car covers exactly 8m every 10s, maintaining equal distances in equal time intervals.

questions.question: Modern quartz wristwatches do not use a swinging pendulum. How do they keep accurate time?

options.text: Using oscillating quartz crystals that vibrate at precise frequencies

questions.explanation: When subjected to an electric current, quartz vibrates at highly consistent, measurable frequencies.

questions.question: Why are atomic clocks considered the most accurate timekeepers in human history?

options.text: They measure time based on the ultra-consistent microwave vibrations of specific atoms

questions.explanation: Atomic resonance is so stable that these clocks lose only about one second over millions of years.

questions.question: If a cyclist takes exactly 50 minutes to cover a distance of 15 km, what is their average speed in m/s?
